  <item>
   <title>Spire collapses at historic Limoges town hall amid violent protests across France</title>
   <link>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/18/spire-collapses-at-historic-limoges-town-hall-amid-violent-protests-across-france</link>
   <guid>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/18/spire-collapses-at-historic-limoges-town-hall-amid-violent-protests-across-france</guid>
   <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 08:25:37 +0200</pubDate>
   <description>Major protests taking place across France on Saturday turned violent in a number of parts of the country as demonstrators clashed with police. Authorities said around 550,000 people took part in the protests nationwide.</description>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>Look, no hands: Euronews rode driverless in Europe's first robotaxi in Zagreb</title>
   <link>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/18/look-no-hands-euronews-rode-driverless-in-europes-first-robotaxi-in-zagreb</link>
   <guid>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/18/look-no-hands-euronews-rode-driverless-in-europes-first-robotaxi-in-zagreb</guid>
   <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 08:00:55 +0200</pubDate>
   <description>The US firm’s robotaxi service is up and running in Zagreb in partnership with local company Verne and Chinese AI firm Pony.ai, a partnership that plans to expand across Europe. Euronews got to see how it works firsthand in Croatia.</description>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>Leisure out of reach for one in eight people in the EU: Where is the problem biggest?</title>
   <link>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/18/leisure-out-of-reach-for-one-in-eight-people-in-the-eu-where-is-the-problem-biggest</link>
   <guid>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/18/leisure-out-of-reach-for-one-in-eight-people-in-the-eu-where-is-the-problem-biggest</guid>
   <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 07:54:13 +0200</pubDate>
   <description>From sport to cinema trips, regular leisure activities are out of reach for around 46 million people in the EU. Income helps explain the gap between countries, but it does not tell the whole story.</description>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>‘Every sunny surface’ is being put to work. Europeans transforming their homes with solar driveways</title>

      <description><p>A girl called Àìná was captured by an African king and later taken to England to become Sarah Forbes Bonetta, protege of the imperial monarch </p><p>When she was seven years old, Bayo Randle’s great-great-grandmother Sarah Forbes Bonetta was presented to Queen Victoria at Windsor Castle as a “diplomatic gift” from an African king.</p><p>Victoria would go on to pay for Bonetta’s education, approve her marriage to one of west Africa’s wealthiest men, and become godmother to her eldest daughter.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/sarah-forbes-bonetta-biography-queen-victoria">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch</link>
      <description><p>At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports</p><p>Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a <a href="https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/12/senegal-brutal-crackdown-violates-lgbt-peoples-rights">new report</a>.</p><p>More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, <a href="https://www.hivjustice.net/cases/senegal-crackdown-on-lgbtq-people-intensifies-with-multiple-arrests/">according to HIV Justice Network</a>, an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial</link>
      <description><p>Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/guinea-bissau">Guinea-Bissau</a> has not approved the controversial <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/hepatitis-b">hepatitis B</a> study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday.</p><p>The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/oct/09/vaccine-trial-guinea-bissau-rfk-jr</link>
      <description><p>Recommended dose of hepatitis B vaccine will be withheld from thousands of newborns by Danish researchers</p><p>A controversial research trial that will withhold hepatitis B vaccines from some African newborns was given approval to move forward this week.</p><p>It is a central part of the vaccine vision for Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime vaccine opponent.</p><p>This article was amended on 13 October 2026. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 07:19:52 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Asia / Pacific</category><title>Months-long Indonesia wildfires spew toxic haze across Southeast Asia</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20261018-months-long-indonesia-wildfires-spew-toxic-haze-across-southeast-asia</link><description>
Parts of southern Southeast Asia have been put under the highest-level haze alert as wildfires that have swept Indonesia for months continue to belch toxic smoke across the region. The seasonal wildfires are worse this year due to the drought conditions caused by a severe "super-El Nino" effect.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/959c6e42-cab9-11f1-bcc1-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-25T172531Z-1337943422-RC29QNASKLJ4-RTRMADP-3-ASIA-WEATHER-INDONESIA-WILDFIRE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/959c6e42-cab9-11f1-bcc1-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-25T172531Z-1337943422-RC29QNASKLJ4-RTRMADP-3-ASIA-WEATHER-INDONESIA-WILDFIRE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e45050c0-caba-11f1-85b5-bd1110e119fe</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 06:30:35 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/959c6e42-cab9-11f1-bcc1-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-25T172531Z-1337943422-RC29QNASKLJ4-RTRMADP-3-ASIA-WEATHER-INDONESIA-WILDFIRE.jpg">© Abriansyah Liberto, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Asia / Pacific</category><title>India's 'cockroach' movement founder released from police custody</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20261018-india-s-cockroach-movement-founder-released-from-police-custody</link><description>
Indian police released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke from detention on Saturday after the activist was detained ahead of a rally calling for the resignation of India's chief election commissioner. Two other CJP leaders remain in custody after having been arrested while demonstrating at a protest site that police had ruled off-limits.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b8ff30cc-cab4-11f1-8c54-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3KJ7R8.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b8ff30cc-cab4-11f1-8c54-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3KJ7R8.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6df91d22-cab4-11f1-9715-9b17793e8591</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 05:47:00 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b8ff30cc-cab4-11f1-8c54-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3KJ7R8.jpg">© Arun Sankar, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Live: A 'record' 855 people detained in Paris during protests, police say</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261018-live-vance-blames-immigration-for-violence-during-protests-in-france</link><description>
Police in Paris said Sunday they had detained a "record figure" of 855 people in the capital during the demonstrations that swept France the day before. The police prefecture added that 13 police officers and gendarmes had been injured during the clashes that broke out on the margins of the mass demonstrations. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3da235f0-cac3-11f1-8679-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3LN4P6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3da235f0-cac3-11f1-8679-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3LN4P6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">537a7882-caa1-11f1-a119-73fa622837ec</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 03:09:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3da235f0-cac3-11f1-8679-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3LN4P6.jpg">© Guillaume Saligot, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Americas</category><title>Rubio says Trump to 'analyze' global impact of Russia sanctions during pause</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261018-rubio-says-trump-russia-sanctions-waiver-designed-to-analyze-global-impact</link><description>
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sanctions and tariffs on Russia would last 60 days, as the move drew bipartisan criticism and raised fears in Ukraine that Washington could ease further restrictions on Moscow.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b46d8a0-c7e7-11f1-819e-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/dcd8c89867be21a42771dcc4bb966f7a0278e690.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b46d8a0-c7e7-11f1-819e-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/dcd8c89867be21a42771dcc4bb966f7a0278e690.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">25029a10-ca9d-11f1-aa47-9186c059e688</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 02:39:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b46d8a0-c7e7-11f1-819e-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/dcd8c89867be21a42771dcc4bb966f7a0278e690.jpg">© Mark Schiefelbein, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Americas</category><title>‘Standing up for democracy’: Atlanta ‘No Kings’ rally draws Trump critics ahead of midterms</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261018-standing-up-for-democracy-atlanta-no-kings-rally-draws-trump-critics-ahead-of-us-midterms</link><description>
“No Kings, Vote Now” was the theme of a rally in Atlanta, one of many organised across the US on Saturday. While many demonstrators denounced President Donald Trump’s policies, organisers said the rally was aimed at getting out the vote in the November 3 midterm elections and protecting democracy in America.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f5ef54b2-ca8c-11f1-b97e-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26290606906702.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f5ef54b2-ca8c-11f1-b97e-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26290606906702.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">174d7436-ca8d-11f1-b7da-d91d395a4215</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 01:50:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f5ef54b2-ca8c-11f1-b97e-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26290606906702.jpg">© Jose Luis Magana, AP</source><dc:creator>Leela JACINTO</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Islamabad has sought to pressure the Afghan Taliban into acting against armed groups attacking Pakistan, but the bombings and diplomatic deadlock have raised fears of a protracted conflict.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/17/escalation-between-pakistan-and-afghanistan-leads-to-heavy-human-toll_6758716_4.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/10/17/escalation-between-pakistan-and-afghanistan-leads-to-heavy-human-toll_6758716_4.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/10/11/1032/0/8256/4128/644/322/60/0/649dd0a_upload-1-arbqhus6wkej-dsf4116.jpg"><media:description type="plain">Abdulraouf Shahed and his son visited the graves of their relatives, killed in a Pakistani airstrike on October 1, 2026, at the Pashad cemetery in Kunar province, eastern Afghanistan, on October 5, 2026.</media:description><media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Sandra Calligaro/item for « LE MONDE »</media:credit></media:content></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Sat, 17 Oct 2026 14:49:01 +0000 en <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion ]]>

On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch.

The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff.

Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

Why it mattered

For the International Space Station to be able to sustain a continuous human occupancy, periodic cargo deliveries are needed. Russia fulfills part of this requirement with its Progress spacecraft, and both ESA (European Space Agency) and JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) have contributed with their Automated Transfer Vehicle (ATV) and H-II Transfer Vehicle (HTV), respectively.

For its part, NASA contracted with Orbital (today, Northrop Grumman) and SpaceX to fly commercial resupply service missions. Both were needed to keep the U.S. operating segment of the station well supplied and with the science and research materials needed for the crew's work.

Below is a video of the explosion

Though adjustments can be made to go without one or more of these vehicles for a short period of time, the Progress, Cygnus and Dragon are key components of the ISS's continuous operation. So returning a vehicle to flight after a catastrophic exploration is important to well-being of the International Space Station program.

As it happened, Antares would fly another 12 times before having to stand down again to be redesigned, but that is for a different This Day in Space entry.

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Lanterns' shocking finale left us with a lot of unanswered questions for a potential season 2 ]]> HBO and HBO Max's "Lanterns" served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were.

While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling.

After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

Warning: Major Spoilers For "Lanterns" Season 1 Ahead!

One of "Lanterns"' standout achievements is revealing the true costs of superheroism by deconstructing its DNA and examining the ugly guts of it all.

It dives into the fear, trauma, and seduction that drive humans to take up the serious business of protecting the universe and doling out justice against both Earth-bound evil and intergalactic threats. "Lanterns" also explores mental health issues and PTSD that are the inevitable byproducts of a life of unimaginable violence. ]]> <![CDATA[ The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect ]]> The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know.

When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars?

Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky.

The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower. Remember to use a trusted website like Time and Date to discover the exact moment of moonset for your location.

Where should I look to see Orionid meteors?

Orionid shooting stars will appear to originate from a patch of sky, or radiant, located close to the red giant star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion, which glistens above the southeastern horizon for stargazers in the U.S. during the early hours of Oct. 22.

For the best views look 40-90 degrees away from the radiant, where the glowing trains left in the wake of the fast-moving meteors will be at their longest. Be sure to head away from artificial lights and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to fully adapt to the dark for the best

What causes the Orionid meteor shower?

The Orionid meteor shower is active each year as Earth passes through the stream of debris left behind by Comet 1P/Halley, which was observed by a fleet of spacecraft when it last visited the inner solar system in 1986.

Shooting stars become visible when particles of the ancient comet collide with our planet's atmosphere at 147,600 miles per hour (237,539 kilometers per hour), vaporizing in a spectacular display of natural fireworks.

Hoping to catch a shooting star for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide to photographing meteor showers, along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'It really does change you': SpaceX Crew-12 commander wishes we could all see our fragile Earth from space ]]> The astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station wish that we could all see Earth as they just did.

An orbital view reveals the immense beauty of our blue planet, the only world we know of that hosts life. But it also highlights how fragile that life is, tethered to our lonely Earth in the vast void of space, according to Crew-12 commander Jessica Meir of NASA.

"You see this very thin, tenuous band of an atmosphere, and you know that that is all that is supporting life, and we really need to do our best to protect it," Meir said on Thursday afternoon (Oct. 15), during a press conference that discussed the recently concluded Crew-12 mission.

"I wish that I could bring all the eyes of all the humans to look back at the Earth in this extraordinary way that we are so privileged to have," she added. "I think it really does change you philosophically and [in] how you see each other, how you see yourself, how you see the human race when you look on it down from the vantage point that we have from above — you know, [it] gives everybody this understanding that we need to protect our planet, that it's not only so beautiful, but it's so precious."

From the International Space Station (ISS), Meir said, it's clear that everything on Earth is connected — and that the borders we've laid down between states and nations are artificial constructs.

"You realize that we really are one human when you are in space," she said. "I wish I could share that perspective with all the eyes of all the humans. I think it would be a very healthy thing for everyone to understand.

Crew-12 mission specialist Andrey Fedyaev, of the Russian space agency Roscosmos, voiced similar sentiments, though he would turn an ISS visitor's eyes inward, to focus on the crew.

"I always say that the life of crewmembers on board the space station is the best example of how people need to live on Earth," Fedyaev said during Thursday's briefing (in Russian; in interpreter translated his words into English in real time)."

"We don't have borders. We are all friendly. We're just one crew, and the safety of the crew, the safety of the station, depends on the actions of the entire crew," he added. "So, if humankind does arrive at the same conclusion — that our Earth, our planet, is one and the same space vessel that flies through space — we need to take care of it and not to destroy it. So, that's what I would like to show to everyone on Earth."

Meir and Fedyaev are far from the only ones to have their perpsectives shifted by a space mission. Pretty much every astronaut experiences this phenomenon, which is known as the overview effect, a term coined in 1987 by space philosopher Frank White.

Crew-12 consisted of Meir, Fedyaev, NASA astronaut Jack Hathaway (the mission's pilot) and the European Space Agency's Sophie Adenot (mission specialist). It was the second spaceflight for Meir and Fedyaev and the first for Hathaway and Adenot.

The quartet launched toward the ISS on Feb. 13 atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Their Crew Dragon capsule, named Freedom, arrived at the orbiting lab a day later.

Crew-12 spent nearly eight months aboard the ISS, finally returning to Earth on Oct. 8. They conducted a wide range of scientific experiments and maintenance work during that time and set a few records as well.

For example, Adenot became the first French woman ever to perform a spacewalk, and she broke the mark for longest continuous spaceflight by a European at 237 days. The previous record, 201 days, was set by Luca Parmitano in 2019-2020.

]]> <![CDATA[ When not to watch a meteor shower — why I'm not staying up for the Orionids ]]> I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective.

The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet, which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside. However, another object is in the sky this year — a big, bright waxing gibbous moon that will brighten the night sky and make "shooting stars" very hard to see.

That doesn't make the Orionids unobservable. In fact, there is a narrow window when the night sky will be free from moonlight. But it does make me far less inclined to sacrifice an entire night for them, and I certainly won't be trying to spend the night camping under a dark sky in a remote rural location far from light pollution. I've discovered that knowing when not to observe is an underrated stargazing skill.

What's happening and when to look

The Orionids are active from Oct. 2 through Nov. 7, with their 2026 maximum expected overnight on Oct. 21-22. They appear to radiate from a point near Orion, although the meteors themselves can streak across almost any part of the sky.

The shower happens because Earth crosses a stream of debris left behind by Halley's Comet, which was last in the inner solar system in 1986 and will return in 2061. Those tiny particles hit our atmosphere at roughly 41 miles (66 kilometers) per second, making Orionids particularly fast meteors.

Under ideal conditions, the International Meteor Organization gives the shower a zenithal hourly rate of 20 or more around maximum. But "zenithal hourly rate" is not the same as promising that I will personally see 20 meteors while standing in my backyard for an hour. It assumes an excellent dark sky, a well-placed radiant and unobstructed viewing. In reality, that's impossible — at the very least you'd have to have eyes in the back of your head. And on each side.

This year adds another complication. The moon reaches first quarter on Oct. 18 and continues waxing toward full on Oct. 26. On the peak night of the Orionids, an 80%-illuminated waxing gibbous moon will be in the night sky as it gets dark on Oct. 21 and sets around 03:00 a.m. local time across Europe and North America on Oct. 22. You can probably see the workaround. Sunrise is roughly 06:30 a.m. local time, which means astronomical darkness — when the sun is more than 18 degrees below the horizon, meaning complete darkness — lasts until around 05:00 a.m. local time (these times work as a ballpark, but you can (check the exact times of moonset and sunrise for your location on Time and Date).

So there is a dark window before dawn, and that is when I would try to see the shower if I were determined to see it. The Orionid radiant is also much better placed after midnight than it is in the evening.

Knowing exactly what's going to happen in the sky turns a casual meteor watch into a rather more calculated exercise.

How and when I'm watching it

My plan for the Orionids this year is the same as usual — after checking the moon phase and the moonset and sunrise times, there's one more variable. The weather forecast first.

If the forecast is excellent and I'm feeling enthusiastic, I'll target the period after moonset and before morning twilight on Oct. 22. If it's due to be cloudy, I'm staying in bed.

This sounds obvious, but I think beginners are sometimes given the impression that successful stargazing requires heroic commitment. It doesn't. A meteor shower is not a performance that disappears the moment the advertised "peak" passes. The Orionids have a relatively broad period of activity, so meteors can appear on nights either side of maximum, too.

If I do go outside at 3:00 a.m., I'll do so without two hugely valuable resources for meteor showers — a lawn chair and bags of patience.

Stargazer's corner: October 16-22, 2026

The moon reaches first quarter on Oct. 18, making stargazing tricky this week. That means I'm changing what I observe rather than declaring the week a write-off. The moon itself becomes an excellent target in early evening around first quarter. Sunlight strikes the lunar landscape along the terminator — the boundary between lunar day and night — throwing mountains and crater rims into strong relief. A cheap pair of binoculars can reveal a surprising amount. With a telescope, you can spend hours getting lost in the Montes Apenninus mountain range and three nearby craters — Eratosthenes and Archimedes on either side, and Plato above. Saturn remains another easy evening target after its Oct. 4 opposition. Look toward the eastern and southeastern sky after dark for its steady yellowish light. Even a modest telescope pointed at Saturn's rings will astound.

Constellation of the week: Cassiopeia

Cassiopeia is one of the easiest constellations I know to find because its five main stars form a conspicuous W — or, right now, something that looks suspiciously more like an M. Look toward the northern sky in the evening. From mid-northern latitudes, Cassiopeia is high and prominent during autumn, on the opposite side of Polaris from the Big Dipper. That relationship is more useful to me than memorizing exactly which way the W should point. Cassiopeia circles Polaris as Earth rotates, so its orientation changes through the night. From sufficiently northerly locations, it's circumpolar, meaning it never sets below the horizon.

Under ideal conditions, the International Meteor Organization gives the shower a zenithal hourly rate of 20 or more around maximum. But "zenithal hourly rate" is not the same as promising that I will personally see 20 meteors while standing in my backyard for an hour. It assumes an excellent dark sky, a well-placed radiant and unobstructed viewing. In reality, that's impossible — at the very least you'd have to have eyes in the back of your head. And on each side.

This year adds another complication. The moon reaches first quarter on Oct. 18 and continues waxing toward full on Oct. 26. On the peak night of the Orionids, an 80%-illuminated waxing gibbous moon will be in the night sky as it gets dark on Oct. 21 and sets around 03:00 a.m. local time across Europe and North America on Oct. 22. You can probably see the workaround. Sunrise is roughly 06:30 a.m. local time, which means astronomical darkness — when the sun is more than 18 degrees below the horizon, meaning complete darkness — lasts until around 05:00 a.m. local time (these times work as a ballpark, but you can (check the exact times of moonset and sunrise for your location on Time and Date).

So there is a dark window before dawn, and that is when I would try to see the shower if I were determined to see it. The Orionid radiant is also much better placed after midnight than it is in the evening.

Knowing exactly what's going to happen in the sky turns a casual meteor watch into a rather more calculated exercise.

How and when I'm watching it

My plan for the Orionids this year is the same as usual — after checking the moon phase and the moonset and sunrise times, there's one more variable. The weather forecast first.

If the forecast is excellent and I'm feeling enthusiastic, I'll target the period after moonset and before morning twilight on Oct. 22. If it's due to be cloudy, I'm staying in bed.

This sounds obvious, but I think beginners are sometimes given the impression that successful stargazing requires heroic commitment. It doesn't. A meteor shower is not a performance that disappears the moment the advertised "peak" passes. The Orionids have a relatively broad period of activity, so meteors can appear on nights either side of maximum, too.

If I do go outside at 3:00 a.m., I'll do so without two hugely valuable resources for meteor showers — a lawn chair and bags of patience.

Stargazer's corner: October 16-22, 2026

The moon reaches first quarter on Oct. 18, making stargazing tricky this week. That means I'm changing what I observe rather than declaring the week a write-off. The moon itself becomes an excellent target in early evening around first quarter. Sunlight strikes the lunar landscape along the terminator — the boundary between lunar day and night — throwing mountains and crater rims into strong relief. A cheap pair of binoculars can reveal a surprising amount. With a telescope, you can spend hours getting lost in the Montes Apenninus mountain range and three nearby craters — Eratosthenes and Archimedes on either side, and Plato above. Saturn remains another easy evening target after its Oct. 4 opposition. Look toward the eastern and southeastern sky after dark for its steady yellowish light. Even a modest telescope pointed at Saturn's rings will astound.

Constellation of the week: Cassiopeia

Cassiopeia is one of the easiest constellations I know to find because its five main stars form a conspicuous W — or, right now, something that looks suspiciously more like an M. Look toward the northern sky in the evening. From mid-northern latitudes, Cassiopeia is high and prominent during autumn, on the opposite side of Polaris from the Big Dipper. That relationship is more useful to me than memorizing exactly which way the W should point. Cassiopeia circles Polaris as Earth rotates, so its orientation changes through the night. From sufficiently northerly locations, it's circumpolar, meaning it never sets below the horizon.

]]> <![CDATA[ How to see the Orionid meteor shower 2026 peak this week — and when to look ]]> If you love watching meteors, 2026 has given you plenty to enjoy. This summer, the annual Perseid meteor shower peaked on the day of a new moon — and a solar eclipse — so moonlight stayed out of the way. And there's more to look forward to: in December, the Geminids, the year's most prolific shower, will peak after a waxing crescent moon sets early in the evening, opening the door to excellent viewing.

Right between those two headline showers, the dependable Orionids take their turn, reaching peak activity around Oct. 21-22.

So, when and where can you catch the show?

When and where to watch

The Orionids take their name from the spot where they seem to fan out: Orion's raised club, just above and to the left of the reddish star Betelgeuse. Orion is usually a winter favorite, so in early autumn the mighty hunter doesn't fully clear the eastern horizon until after 11 p.m. local daylight time. Don't rush outside just yet though. Wait until around 2 a.m., when Orion is well above the horizon. By about 5 a.m., just before dawn, Orion reaches its highest point in the southern sky — and the view should be at its best.

Orionid meteors tend to be faint, so city lights can easily wash them out. If you can, head to a safe, dark rural spot. Get comfortable in a reclining lawn chair or sleeping bag, give your eyes time to adjust, and enjoy the view overhead and toward the southern sky.

Why the moon won't spoil the show

And what about the moon? A full moon arrives October 25-26, but there's still a welcome stretch of dark sky for several mornings before Wednesday.

By Oct. 21-22, the waxing gibbous moon will be resting among the dim stars of Capricornus, reaching its highest point around 8:45 p.m. local daylight time. Here's the good news: it will set shortly after 2 a.m., leaving roughly 3½ hours of dark sky before dawn. In that window, one observer may spot as many as 15 to 20 Orionids per hour. Because those hours line up with the shower's peak, the moon shouldn't steal the show this year.

Halley's Comet: the source of the Orionids

So, where do the Orionids come from? Their story begins with Halley's Comet—the same famous visitor behind May's Eta Aquarids.

Meteoroids are tiny leftovers from a comet's nucleus. As a comet nears the sun, frozen material on its surface turns directly into gas, a process known as sublimation. The comet becomes a kind of cosmic litterbug, sprinkling dust and debris along its orbit. Those pieces are tiny and brittle, with the consistency of cigar ash, and every swing past the sun leaves more behind.

Comets are among the solar system's oldest and most fascinating objects. They formed alongside the sun and planets about 4.6 billion years ago, yet they have changed remarkably little. Think of them as time capsules from the solar system's childhood. Far beyond the outer planets, they spend most of their time in a deep freeze, where temperatures hover just above absolute zero, -459.67°F (-273.15°C). In that extreme cold, chemical reactions largely stop, helping comets preserve material from those earliest days.

Over the past 100,000 years, Halley's Comet has probably circled the sun well over a thousand times, leaving a fresh trail of debris on every visit. Each October and May, Earth brushes close to Halley's orbit. Some of that dust meets our atmosphere at a breathtaking 41 miles (66 km) per second, lighting up as the streaks we call "shooting stars."

The Orionids have another lovely feature: about half of these meteors leave glowing trails that linger longer than those of equally bright meteors. Halley's composition may be the reason. The particles begin burning up about 80 miles (130 km) above Earth, perhaps because they're made of lightweight material from the comet's diffuse surface rather than its core.

Looking backward . . . and forward

Perhaps you remember seeing Halley's Comet when it last swept through the inner solar system in late winter and early spring of 1986. With an orbital period of 75.4 years, this celebrated visitor is due back in late July or early August 2061.

For a little perspective, average life expectancy is 79.5 years in the United States, 82.2 years in the United Kingdom, and 83.4 years in Canada. So, if you were born after 1980, there's a fair chance you'll be here to welcome the "mother of all Orionids" home in 2061.

As for me, I saw Halley in 1986 at the "advanced age" of 30. The odds of another reunion are pretty long — you can do the math.

Until then, I'll be more than happy to step outside early on Wednesday morning and greet a few of "Halley's children." I hope you'll join me.

Joe Rao serves as an instructor and guest lecturer at New York's Hayden Planetarium. He writes about astronomy for Natural History magazine, Sky and Telescope, The Old Farmer's Almanac and other publications.

]]> <![CDATA[ Scientists find 'gemstones' in atmosphere of bizarre, scorching-hot 'marshmallow' exoplanet ]]> Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow.

The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST, is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this "hot Jupiter" skyrocket.

Given the extreme conditions of this exoplanet, it is little wonder that its atmosphere is pretty unusual too. Using a new technique called transmission strings, a team of scientists mapped the contours of the atmosphere of WASP-17b. They found that the atmosphere is shaped like a ring with prominent "gems" rising from it.

"Planets are temperamental, their atmospheres complex and chaotic," team member Hannah Wakeford of the University of Bristol said in a statement. "The fact that all of these numbers came together and showed us this very structured, dynamical picture of this giant world over 1,000 light-years away was just really exciting."

Astronomers like WASP-17b so much they put a ring on it

WASP-17b is so close to its parent star that it is tidally locked, meaning one side permanently faces the star; its dayside is constantly bombarded with stellar radiation. In contrast, the planet also has a cooler nightside, which faces out into space in perpetuity.

By creating incredibly comprehensive 3D views of this exoplanet's atmosphere, researchers found that WASP-17b's atmosphere has a chemical composition and temperature that shift between dayside and nightside according to theory and modelling.

This was possible because the transmission strings technique tracked WASP-17b as it crossed or transited in front of its star, capturing the composition of light around the edge of the planet's atmosphere, or limb, from different angles. This method trumps standard approaches because traditional modelling only maps light as an average across the entire limb.

"Rather than assuming your atmosphere is a circle with the same radius all the way around, our technique allows you to pull out different distances from the center to the edge of the planet," Lili Alderson, of Cornell University, said. "We're able to go around the edge.

"So, we've gone from a ring to understanding where on the ring the gemstones are, so to speak."

The modelling showed just such a "gem," that occurs where hot winds from the planet reach the equator and the nightside of WASP-17b, the atmosphere of the cooler side inflates.

"Theory predicts that the morning and the evening sides should have a strong temperature difference, and WASP-17b fits really nicely in that trend – pretty much bang-on what we thought it would be," Alderson said.

The successful application of the transmission strings method is an exciting step forward in the modelling of the atmospheres of the over 6,000 worlds in NASA's exoplanet catalog.

"This is proof of concept that planets are, in fact, 3D objects, and that, consistently, as they go around their star, what we predict should be happening is happening," Alderson concluded. "To move beyond computational exercises and see it for real is a different matter."

The team's research was published on Wednesday (Oct.14) in the journal Nature Astronomy.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX thrusters just made a Tesla Roadster 'fly' (and Elon Musk's car is still out there in space) ]]>

Well, that was a memorable debut.

Tesla unveiled its highly anticipated new Roadster last night (Oct. 16) with a spectacular stunt, using SpaceX thrusters to make the vehicle "fly."

"This is not necessarily a safety-optimized car, OK?" Elon Musk, who runs both companies, said during the livestreamed reveal, which was held at SpaceX's rocket-testing facility in McGregor, Texas. "But it takes the the fun meter to 11 out of 10."

Tesla first announced the next-gen Roadster in 2017, saying at the time that it would be released in 2020. In 2018, Musk announced that the new car would incorporate some SpaceX tech.

"SpaceX option package for new Tesla Roadster will include ~10 small rocket thrusters arranged seamlessly around car. These rocket engines dramatically improve acceleration, top speed, braking & cornering. Maybe they will even allow a Tesla to fly…" he wrote on Twitter in June of that year. (In 2022, Musk bought Twitter, which he subsequently renamed X.)

So last night's demonstration didn't come entirely out of left field — but it was still eye-popping. The show began with the Roadster driving up a ramp that quickly became a vertical wall and then an overhanging ledge. The Roadster clung to the surface, hanging upside-down from the ledge like a gecko on a ceiling thanks to a special fan suction system on its chassis.

"I mean, this car really sucks, OK?" Musk said, channeling his inner stand-up comedian. "This car could suck the chrome off a trailer hitch. It could suck a tennis ball through a hose pipe."

The suction feature is not just a novelty, he added: It will help the Roadster stay connected to the ground during high-speed turns, allowing drivers to corner incredibly well.

And the sucking was just an opening act. The Tesla soon launched itself from its position beneath the ramp's nearly horizontal ledge, executed a barrel roll in midair, and landed softly, all thanks to its SpaceX cold-gas thrusters.

"A friend of mine, Peter Thiel, once said that the future promised us flying cars, but instead we got 140 characters," Musk said after the Roadster touched down. "Well, not anymore."

The car has main thrusters in the rear, he explained, as well as attitude-control thrusters that control its orientation.

"So it can basically fly like a rocket, and it could do rolls," Musk said. "It could do, like, crazy gymnastics — whatever you want, really."

The Roadster has a total of 10 thrusters, which are fed by 600 liters — about 250 kilograms (550 pounds) — of compressed air, Tesla Engineering Vice President Lars Moravy said during last night's event. That air is housed in carbon fiber overwrapped pressure vessels, which fill "every usable void in the car," Tesla said via X last night.

The Tesla team put those thrusters to work multiple times during the presentation, at one point launching the Roadster over a line of six vehicles, including a Tesla semi-truck cab.

Nobody was behind the wheel during these stunts — nobody with a pulse, anyway. The driver's seat was occupied by a mannequin clad in a black-and-white SpaceX spacesuit.

This was a nod to "Starman," the dummy behind the wheel of Musk's cherry-red first-gen Roadster, which launched into orbit around the sun in February 2018 on the first-ever flight of SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket.

Starman and his Roadster are still in space, by the way, and will be for a while. Modeling work suggests the duo will keep orbiting our star for millions of years before ultimately slamming into either Earth or Venus.

Last night's Roadster demo was something of a tease, for the car is not yet in showrooms. Musk said Tesla aims to begin producing it in 2028.

And don't expect to see the "flying" version on the road then, or anytime; it's hard to imagine regulators certifying that vehicle for everyday use. It will likely be a status symbol for a few wealthy and connected folks, locked away in spacious and well-appointed garages.

Indeed, you can't put down on a deposit for the "Rocket" version of the new Roadster on Tesla's website; purchase of that vehicle is by invite only.

Two other Roadster versions are for sale — "Performance" and "Thrust." Tesla's website describes the Performance variant as "road ready," with "active aero and a multi-mode suction system." Thrust, by contrast, is "race ready." It has active aero and suction "plus acceleration thrusters."

It costs $50,000 to reserve a Performance vehicle and $250,000 to reserve a Thrust. Tesla has not yet revealed the total cost of any of the new Roadster variants.

 <title>ONLINE: Jen jedna žena z 27 zvolených. Letošní volby přinesly historicky nejnižší počet senátorek</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/online-jen-jedna-zena-z-27-zvolenych-letosni-volby-prinesly-historicky-nejnizsi_2610180753_med</link>
 <description>Senátní volby jsou u konce. Vítězem letošního hlasování se stalo hnutí STAN, které získalo deset senátorských křesel. Sedm mandátů připadlo ODS. Naopak vládní hnutí ANO nezískalo ani jedno křeslo, přestože do druhého kola postoupilo třináct jeho kandidátů. Opoziční strany si tak v horní komoře Parlamentu udržely většinu. Volební účast ve druhém kole dosáhla 21,12 procenta, což je nejvíce od roku 2010. </description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-114410832_261017-192127_kvr.jpg?itok=-_k4Que-" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 07:53:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Politoložka: Babiš má problém, kandidáti ANO neměli servis. Lídrem opozice se teď cítí víc lidí</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/politolozka-babis-ma-problem-kandidati-ano-nemeli-servis-lidrem-opozice-se-ted_2610180625_med</link>
 <description>Životabudič pro opozici, katastrofa pro ANO. Jak Grolich, Papoušek, Smoljak a další ovládli senátní volby? Kvůli čemu tak uspěl STAN? A proč Babišovi kandidáti selhali?</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/9966864c57974e5252665228e6b581f6.jpg?itok=VuecHp3P" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 06:25:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Komunisté v komunále přišli o většinu mandátů. Nezachránili ani tradiční bašty na Karvinsku</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/komuniste-v-komunale-prisli-o-vetsinu-mandatu-nezachranili-ani-tradicni-basty-na_2610180600_pik</link>
 <description>Poté, co komunisté ztratili v roce 2021 zastoupení v celostátní politice, přišla teď v komunálních volbách další rána. Podle analýzy datového týmu Českého rozhlasu přišla KSČM i o zastoupení ve dvou třetinách obcí a měst a ztratila tři čtvrtiny všech svých mandátů. Nepodržely je ani tradiční bašty ve Slezsku a na severu Čech. Podle politologa Jakuba Lyska představují tyto výsledky pro stranu „debakl“ a věstí po sto letech existence její konec.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-077479190_250728-083227_mst.jpg?itok=9sx0bH63" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 06:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Voliči poslouchají Babišovy signály. A v tom tkví problém ANO v senátních volbách, popisuje odborník</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/volici-poslouchaji-babisovy-signaly-a-v-tom-tkvi-problem-ano-v-senatnich-volbach_2610180500_jgr</link>
 <description>Opozice se pro senátní volby spojila a jasně zvítězila. Prorektor Metropolitní univerzity Praha Petr Just vidí za jednoznačnou prohrou hnutí ANO i to, že jeho voliči vnímali signály, které vysílal Andrej Babiš. „Zřejmě si neuvědomoval, že jak Senát napadal, tak se to pak propsalo i do nálad jeho voličů,“ popisuje v rozhovoru pro iROZHLAS.cz politolog. A rozebírá mimo jiné i to, co může stát za tím, že o svou jedinou senátorku přišli i Piráti.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-104205070_261017-202041_jgr.jpg?itok=5N2b0lZ7" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 05:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>ANO nedodrželo sliby a nepřitahuje zajímavé figury. STAN je má, ale nevíme, co čekat, říká Zlámalová</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/ano-nedodrzelo-sliby-a-nepritahuje-zajimave-figury-stan-je-ma-ale-nevime-co_2610180010_brz</link>
 <description>Senátní volby ovládlo hnutí STAN, získalo 10 mandátů. Hnutí ANO naopak neproměnilo ani jednu z 13 šancí na úspěch. „Andrej Babiš udělal podle mého názoru před volbami špatně skoro všechno. Postupně začal vyhrožovat lidem i obcím, že jim sebere peníze, a potom i bankám, že na ně uvalí sankce, pokud nebudou dávat levnější hypotéky,“ říká komentátorka Czech News Center Lenka Zlámalová.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/1841d00b6840bb4a2bbdec331c284ef1.jpg?itok=oVFvx5aM" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 00:10:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>VOLEBNÍ MAPY: Podívejte se, jak se měnila podpora kandidátů mezi jednotlivými koly senátních voleb</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/volebni-mapy-podivejte-se-jak-se-menila-podpora-kandidatu-mezi-jednotlivymi-koly_2610172334_pik</link>
 <description>Voliči v Česku vybrali ve zbylých 22 obvodech ty, kteří je budou v horní komoře po příštích šest let reprezentovat. Nejvíce voličů přitáhl i v druhém kole souboj o senátní post v Plzni-městě, kde nakonec vyhrál Karel Řehka (za STAN). Nejméně voličů pak dorazilo podruhé k volebním urnám v obvodu Karviná. Web iROZHLAS.cz ukazuje v mapách, jak se měnila v jednotlivých volebních obvodech podpora senátních kandidátů. Najděte si ten svůj.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/navrh_bez_nazvu_261017-212102_pik.png?itok=h6fO6ceO" type="image/png" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 23:34:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Bývalý šéf armády, propagátor hanáčtiny i dědička klavírního impéria. Poznejte své (staro)nové senátory</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/byvaly-sef-armady-propagator-hanactiny-i-dedicka-klavirniho-imperia-poznejte-sve_2610172211_kvr</link>
 <description>Voliči ve druhém kole voleb ve 22 obvodech vybrali své zástupce v Senátu na příštích šest let. Překvapivě ani jeden mandát nezískalo vládní hnutí ANO, jehož kandidáti nakonec pohořeli i v jinak jisté „baště“ v obvodu Karviná. Do senátních lavic nakonec zamíří i bývalý náčelník generálního štábu Karel Řehka (za STAN) či liberecký hejtman Martin Půta (SLK). Jako jediná žena ve druhém kole uspěla Zuzana Ceralová Petrofová (za ODS).</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-114410265_261017-184728_kvr.jpg?itok=kEqBXPoL" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 22:11:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>

   <description>Jako dítě usínal na pódiu, v devadesátých letech zažíval s The Kelly Family obrovskou slávu a několik let se bez ochranky téměř nemohl pohybovat. Dnes Angelo Kelly žije s rodinou v Irsku, píše osobní písně a vrací se k samostatnému koncertování. V úterý 10. listopadu vystoupí se svou kapelou v pražském Lucerna Music Baru.    <description>Šok pro Slavii. Lídr Chance Ligy v 11. kole jen remizoval doma s Hradcem Králové 0:0. Předvedl se Chorý, který rozhodčímu Všetečkovi ukázal prostředníček a za vulgární gesto byl vyloučen. Druhý Liberec zaváhání Pražanů nevyužil, v Olomouci prohrál 0:1.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Zranění policisté, rabování i požáry. Ve Francii při protestech zadrželi 1 200 lidí</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/francie-protesty-policie-sobota-pariz-demonstrace.A261018_071044_zahranicni_ikro#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Násilnosti, které v sobotu provázely v některých francouzských městech celostátní demonstrace, si vyžádaly 150 zraněných policistů a četníků, 1 200 lidí bylo zadrženo. Oznámil to francouzský premiér Sébastien Lecornu. V Paříži bylo zadrženo rekordních 855 lidí, sdělila policie. V sobotu se v celé Francii konaly demonstrace proti zvyšování životních nákladů. </description>
      <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 07:10:22 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni">Zprávy - Zahraničí</category>
      <comments>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/francie-protesty-policie-sobota-pariz-demonstrace.A261018_071044_zahranicni_ikro/diskuse</comments>

      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/102/cl6/IKR3d7703e8d1_58RMADP_3_FRANCE_PROTEST.JPG" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Proti vysokým životním nákladům v sobotu ve Francii protestovaly statisíce lidí. (17. října 2026)</media:description>
      <media:credit>Reuters</media:credit>
      <media:group>
        <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/102/cl6/IKR3d96909602_51RMADP_3_FRANCE_PROTEST.JPG" type="image/jpeg" />
        <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/102/cl6/ICH8c54319582_p2026101704144.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      </media:group>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Skáču do rozjetého vlaku, ve kterém jsem ještě nebyl. Senátor Řehka o svých cílech</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/volby/plzen/karel-rehka-senator-volby-2026-plzen-mesto-rozhovor.A261017_164136_plzen-volby_jzk#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Nově zvolený senátor za obvod Plzeň-město Karel Řehka slavil vítězství společně s manželkou Michaelou v restauraci v centru Plzně. Soupeřku Lucii Kantorovou z ANO porazil nominant STAN ve druhém kole rozdílem bezmála 20 procent hlasů. „Jsem neskutečně vděčný za důvěru, kterou mi voliči dali,“ byla jeho první slova po sečtení hlasů ze všech volebních okrsků.</description>
      <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/volby/plzen">Plzeň - Plzeň - Volby</category>

      <media:description>Karel Řehka slaví zvolení senátorem. (17. října 2026)</media:description>

    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Amerika má zpoždění. Proč se tam rychlovlaky na rozdíl od Asie neprosadily</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/zahranicni/usa-zeleznice-spojene-staty-vysokorychlostni-trate-vlaky.A261015_180252_eko-zahranicni_jla#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Z Las Vegas do jižní Kalifornie za pouhé dvě hodiny. Takový je plán americké společnosti Brightline, která připravuje výstavbu přibližně 350 kilometrů dlouhé vysokorychlostní tratě. Vlaky by na ní měly dosahovat rychlosti až 320 kilometrů za hodinu. Přestože jsou podobná spojení hlavně v Asii běžná, Spojené státy v tomto segmentu za světem až do této doby výrazně zaostávaly.</description>
      <pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 07:00:00 GMT</pubDate>

      <media:description>Vlakový spoj od společnosti Brightline na Floridě (22. září 2023)</media:description>

    <item>
      <title>Hrozny lepí ruce, slunce pálí. Jak se sklízí na nejvýše položené vinici v Mikulově</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/brno/zpravy/vinobrani-sber-hroznu-vino-vinarstvi-fucik-mikulov-reportaz.A261015_202056_brno-zpravy_azu#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Je odsud dechberoucí výhled do okolí. Přes vinohrad pod známým vrcholem Turold na okraji Mikulova na Břeclavsku by se dalo na krajinu pod sebou dívat i hodiny, zvlášť když zrovna slunce příjemně hřeje a žene venkovní teplotu nahoru. Ale proto tu tentokrát nejsme. Je začátek října a na nejvýše položené mikulovské vinici vrcholí sběr hroznů, které patří pod místní Vinařství Fučík.</description>

      <title>Litva se obávala dronu, vyhlásila červený poplach. Vzlétly stíhačky NATO</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/litva-kratce-vyhlasila-kvuli-dronu-cerveny-stupen-leteckeho-poplachu.A261018_075228_zahranicni_ikro#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Litvav neděli ráno vyhlásila ve středních a severních regionech země červený stupeň leteckého poplachu a jejich obyvatele vyzvala, aby se odebrali do úkrytů. Příčinou byl neznámý letící objekt, oznámila armáda a národní krizové centrum, uvedla agentura Reuters. Zhruba po hodině armáda poplach odvolala.

    <item>
      <title>Vojenskou základnu v Kanadě zachvátil požár. Úřady hlásí mrtvé i raněné</title>

<description>Jednotné měsíční hlá&#353;ení zaměstnavatele (JMHZ) má státu umožnit sbírat dal&#353;í údaje o zaměstnancích a zpřístupnit je více úřadům. Ministerstvo práce a sociálních věcí navrhuje změny, které mají reagovat na novou legislativu i praktické potřeby státních institucí. <link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/americky-groupon-bude-pod-taktovkou-cechu-prodavat-pres-ai-agenty/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Někdej&#353;í internetový fenomén hromadných slev Groupon, který kormidlují Če&#353;i z Pale Fire Capial, se otevřel obchodování, při kterém si zážitky nemají kupovat lidé, ale dělat to za ně mají AI agenti. Nově spu&#353;těná platforma LivingSocial jim umožňuje vyhledávat a porovnávat zážitky a připravit nákup. Nabízí přes 50 tisíc aktivit napříč Spojenými státy.</description>

<title>Česko pomáhá rozhýbat evropský čipový průmysl. Nová služba vývojářům ušetří hromadu práce</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/cesko-pomaha-rozhybat-evropsky-cipovy-prumysl-nova-sluzba-vyvojarum-usetri-hromadu-prace/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český národní polovodičový klastr ve spolupráci s Českým polovodičovým centrem vytvořily užitečný online nástroj. Jde o katalog takzvaných IP bloků používaných při vývoji čipů. Tyto bloky v katalogu nabízí firmy a organizace z Evropy. Cílem je polovodičovým návrhářům nabídnout jednoduchý přístup ke klíčovým technologiím, které jsou ověřené a rychle nasaditelné a není je nutné vynalézat znovu.</description>

<item>
<title>Miliarda jim trvala tři roky, druhá jen pět měsíců. Českou AI naději už používají Meta, Xiaomi nebo Nvidia</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/miliarda-jim-trvala-tri-roky-druha-jen-pet-mesicu-ceskou-ai-nadeji-uz-pouzivaji-meta-xiaomi-nebo-nvidia/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český startup E2B aktuálně patří k největ&#353;ím technologickým nadějím země. Pro AI agenty umožňuje velice rychle spou&#353;tět sandboxy, tedy izolovaná prostředí, v nichž agenti mohou běžet, vykonat práci a sandbox následně ukončit. E2B pokračuje v silném růstu. Firma informovala, že jí trvalo tři roky, než u ní zákazníci rozjeli miliardu sandboxů. Teď pokočila metu dvou miliard sandboxů s tím, že druhá miliarda trvala pouze pět měsíců.</description>

<description>Jednotné měsíční hlá&#353;ení zaměstnavatele (JMHZ) má státu umožnit sbírat dal&#353;í údaje o zaměstnancích a zpřístupnit je více úřadům. <description>Někdej&#353;í internetový fenomén hromadných slev Groupon, který kormidlují Če&#353;i z Pale Fire Capial, se otevřel obchodování, při kterém si zážitky nemají kupovat lidé, ale dělat to za ně mají AI agenti. Nově spu&#353;těná platforma LivingSocial jim umožňuje vyhledávat a porovnávat zážitky a připravit nákup. Nabízí přes 50 tisíc aktivit napříč Spojenými státy.</description>

<title>Česko pomáhá rozhýbat evropský čipový průmysl. Nová služba vývojářům ušetří hromadu práce</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/cesko-pomaha-rozhybat-evropsky-cipovy-prumysl-nova-sluzba-vyvojarum-usetri-hromadu-prace/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český národní polovodičový klastr ve spolupráci s Českým polovodičovým centrem vytvořily užitečný online nástroj. Jde o katalog takzvaných IP bloků používaných při vývoji čipů. Tyto bloky v katalogu nabízí firmy a organizace z Evropy. Cílem je polovodičovým návrhářům nabídnout jednoduchý přístup ke klíčovým technologiím, které jsou ověřené a rychle nasaditelné a není je nutné vynalézat znovu.</description>

<item>
<title>Miliarda jim trvala tři roky, druhá jen pět měsíců. Českou AI naději už používají Meta, Xiaomi nebo Nvidia</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/miliarda-jim-trvala-tri-roky-druha-jen-pet-mesicu-ceskou-ai-nadeji-uz-pouzivaji-meta-xiaomi-nebo-nvidia/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český startup E2B aktuálně patří k největ&#353;ím technologickým nadějím země. Pro AI agenty umožňuje velice rychle spou&#353;tět sandboxy, tedy izolovaná prostředí, v nichž agenti mohou běžet, vykonat práci a sandbox následně ukončit. E2B pokračuje v silném růstu. Firma informovala, že jí trvalo tři roky, než u ní zákazníci rozjeli miliardu sandboxů. Teď pokočila metu dvou miliard sandboxů s tím, že druhá miliarda trvala pouze pět měsíců.</description>

Riziko trvá i na podzim</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903191-stovky-onemocneni-od-klistat-v-libereckem-kraji-riziko-trva-i-na-podzim.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903191-stovky-onemocneni-od-klistat-v-libereckem-kraji-riziko-trva-i-na-podzim.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 07:01:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Za prvních devět měsíců roku bylo v Libereckém kraji hlášeno 31 případů klíšťové encefalitidy a 728 případů lymeské borreliózy. Celkem jde o 759 případů obou infekcí. Podle odborníků ale riziko nakažení trvá i během podzimu.</description></item><item><title>Slovan prohrál v Olomouci 0:1, dva góly mu odvolal VAR</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903315-slovan-prohral-v-olomouci-0-1-dva-goly-mu-odvolal-var.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903315-slovan-prohral-v-olomouci-0-1-dva-goly-mu-odvolal-var.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:23:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Liberečtí fotbalisté v lize podruhé za sebou prohráli a potřetí nedali gól. V Olomouci tedy skórovali hned třikrát, jenže ani jeden z gólů neplatil. A protože branka domácích z 11. minuty byla v pořádku, Slovan prohrál 0:1.</description></item><item><title>Nový senátor Půta se vzdá imunity ve své korupční kauze</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903310-novy-senator-puta-se-vzda-imunity-ve-sve-korupcni-kauze.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903310-novy-senator-puta-se-vzda-imunity-ve-sve-korupcni-kauze.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 17:47:37 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Liberecký hejtman Martin Půta (Starostové pro Liberecký kraj), který byl zvolen do Senátu za obvod Česká Lípa, senátorské imunity nevyužije. Půta je nepravomocně odsouzen v korupční kauze, v níž ale vinu odmítá.</description></item><item><title>Hejtman Půta míří do Senátu, ve druhém kole porazil Jitku Volfovou</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903290-hejtman-puta-miri-do-senatu-ve-druhem-kole-porazil-jitku-volfovou.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903290-hejtman-puta-miri-do-senatu-ve-druhem-kole-porazil-jitku-volfovou.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 15:10:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Senátorem za Českolipsko a část Liberecka a Mělnicka bude v následujícím volebním období dlouholetý hejtman Libereckého kraje Martin Půta (Starostové pro LK). Ten ve druhém kole porazil končící starostku České Lípy Jitku Volfovou (ANO). Ta tak zůstává poslankyní.</description></item><item><title>Místo psychologa chatbot. S AI řeší trápení už třetina dospělých</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903156-misto-psychologa-chatbot-s-ai-resi-trapeni-uz-tretina-dospelych.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903156-misto-psychologa-chatbot-s-ai-resi-trapeni-uz-tretina-dospelych.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 13:25:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Hanka Poskočilová</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Máte trápení? Možná ho dneska dřív než kamarádovi svěříte umělé inteligenci. Podle nového průzkumu už to dělá třetina dospělých a mezi mladými dokonce více než polovina.</description></item><item><title>Kamion v noci zablokoval silnici z Turnova na Malou Skálu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903275-kamion-v-noci-zablokoval-silnici-z-turnova-na-malou-skalu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903275-kamion-v-noci-zablokoval-silnici-z-turnova-na-malou-skalu.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 11:38:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>K dopravní nehodě došlo v noci na sobotu na silnici číslo 10 mezi Turnovem a Malou Skálou. Kamion silnici v Borku zcela zablokoval.</description></item><item><title>Pozor na linky 21 a 56 MHD v Liberci: Zastávka Školní je jinde. Kdy se vrátí zpět?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903238-pozor-na-linky-21-a-56-mhd-v-liberci-zastavka-skolni-je-jinde-kdy-se-vrati-zpet.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903238-pozor-na-linky-21-a-56-mhd-v-liberci-zastavka-skolni-je-jinde-kdy-se-vrati-zpet.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Cestující městskou hromadnou dopravou v Liberci musejí počítat se změnou u linek na Králově háji. Kvůli stavebním pracím došlo v tomto týdnu k přesunu zastávky Školní pro autobusové linky 21 a 56 ve směru do centra. Kde teď zastávku cestující najdou a kdy se vrátí na své původní místo?</description></item><item><title>Zuzana Kocumová vyhrála světový titul ve Spartan sprintu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/903188-zuzana-kocumova-vyhrala-svetovy-titul-ve-spartan-sprintu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/903188-zuzana-kocumova-vyhrala-svetovy-titul-ve-spartan-sprintu.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 09:23:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Ostatní sporty</category><description>Liberecká závodnice a politička Zuzana Kocumová dosáhla v posledních týdnech dvou velkých sportovních úspěchů. Po titulu mistryně Evropy v závodech Spartan ovládla také sprint na světovém šampionátu v chorvatském Hvaru.</description></item><item><title>Zažijte magický sklářský víkend. Křišťálové údolí otevírá přes 50 míst</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903237-zazijte-magicky-sklarsky-vikend-kristalove-udoli-otevira-pres-50-mist.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903237-zazijte-magicky-sklarsky-vikend-kristalove-udoli-otevira-pres-50-mist.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 07:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Nahlédněte pod ruce mistrům sklářům i šperkařům. O tomto víkendu se veřejnosti otvírá více než 50 skláren, ateliérů a muzeí napříč Libereckým krajem. Čekají vás tvořivé dílny, práce u pecí i neopakovatelná atmosféra řemesla zapsaného v UNESCO. Vyrazte za zážitkem a vyrobte si třeba vlastní šperk.</description></item><item><title>Přechod, kde si chodci rozsvítí zelenou sami, navrhl pro Zálesní Lhotu student</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902954-prechod-kde-si-chodci-rozsviti-zelenou-sami-navrhl-pro-zalesni-lhotu-student.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902954-prechod-kde-si-chodci-rozsviti-zelenou-sami-navrhl-pro-zalesni-lhotu-student.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 16 Oct 2026 19:53:00 +0200</pubDate><category>Doprava</category><description>V Zálesní Lhotě na Semilsku slouží od srpna nový přechod se semaforem, který si chodci spouštějí tlačítkem. Navrhl ho student a jeho nápad se proměnil ve skutečné dopravní opatření. Přechod řeší dlouholetý problém na frekventované silnici, kterou denně přecházejí i děti cestou na autobus.</description></item></channel></rss>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Sat, 17 Oct 2026 16:29:52 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Víkend Křišťálového údolí 2 – Den otevřených dveří Sklářského muzea (Kamenický Šenov 2026) https://www.vybezek.eu/295953-vikend-kristaloveho-udoli-2-den-otevrenych-dveri-sklarskeho-muzea-kamenicky-senov-2026/ Sat, 17 Oct 2026 16:29:52 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=295953 Víkend 17. a 18. října 2026 v Libereckém kraji opět ve znamení Křišťálového údolí, znovu se otevřely brány a dveře v mnoha sklárnách, ateliérech, výrobních provozech, muzeích a školách.

Těch míst je plno křížem krážem přes celý kraj. Už dlouho se opakovaně kochávám v Preciose, byl jsem kdysi také v Novém Boru v Crystalexu, a letos jsem si řekl, že nikam nespěchám a když už jsem jednou v Kamenickém Šenově, okouknu zas jednou místní muzeum. Rekonstrukce stále probíhá, takže funguje v minimalistickém režimu. Nicméně poseděl jsem, pokoukal a hlavně pokecal. A i o tom tenhle křišťálový víkend přece má být…
